title: Recovery point objective not stated for the 19 services
source: 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Non Functional Specification v3.docx
description: NFR-022 asks for the maximum data loss the business accepts and gives 'The ACE recovery point objective' as its target, with no value. Architecture v5 splits the Workbench into 19 services and records that the recovery point and recovery time objectives are not set, so there is no value per service either. Version 4 keeps the target, the DL11 decision and the Open status word for word, adds the owning service cell from the Microservice Ownership Map v1, and states the position in the section 3.4 note; no RPO value is written.
evidence: NFR-022 requirement and target 'The ACE recovery point objective'; section 5 row NFR-022 with decision DL11; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 48 'RPO/RTO: not yet set' and note 'NFR gap: RPO/RTO are not set in NFR Spec v3; proposed tiers'; Template and Rules R5.5 (no DP row sets RPO or RTO)
proposed: Confirm one recovery point objective for the 19 Recovery schemas on the ACE PostgreSQL server, with the ACE platform tier as the floor, and replace the target of NFR-022 with it at the next NFR baseline; the value belongs to the failover and restore test of section 3.4

title: Recovery time objective not stated for the 19 services
source: 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Non Functional Specification v3.docx
description: NFR-023 asks for the maximum time to restore service and gives 'The ACE recovery time objective' as its target, with no value and no per-service tier. Architecture v5 records that the objectives are not set and proposes tiers that the extract does not name. Version 4 keeps the target, the DL11 decision and the Open status word for word, adds the owning service cell, and states the position in the section 3.4 note; no RTO value is written.
evidence: NFR-023 requirement and target 'The ACE recovery time objective'; section 5 row NFR-023 with decision DL11; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 48 'RPO/RTO: not yet set' and note 'NFR gap: RPO/RTO are not set in NFR Spec v3; proposed tiers'
proposed: Confirm one recovery time objective with a tier per service wave (0 to 4) and replace the target of NFR-023 with it at the next NFR baseline; the value drives the failover and restore test and the 99.9 percent target of NFR-020

title: 'Weeks' versus '28 days' wording for the same period
source: 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Non Functional Specification v3.docx
description: The NFR set and the design set use two wordings for the same period: 'weeks' for a wait or a retention, and '28 days'. The retention requirements give no period at all (NFR-028 'periods not set', NFR-031 and NFR-075 'Not set', decision DL26), and the only 28 days in the realignment sources is the Temporal Continue-As-New interval of the workflow design, not a retention period. Version 4 keeps every target word for word and states the reading in the section 3.5 note, so a reader does not take 28 days as a retention period.
evidence: NFR-028 target 'Retention classes defined per type; periods not set'; NFR-030, NFR-031 and NFR-075 targets and decision DL26; Recovery Workbench Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 slide 13 'Continue-As-New at each stage end, at least every 28 days'; Recovery Workbench Architecture Decision Records v3 ADR-011 option text 'A wait of weeks is a row with a state and a stored due date'
proposed: Compliance states each retention period in one unit for the document types, the decision log, the case records and the interaction ledger, and the 28 days stays only in the workflow design as the Continue-As-New interval

title: NFR-042 logs reads of a data lake copy that Architecture v5 removes
source: 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Non Functional Specification v3.docx
description: NFR-042 requires that every read of the case store, the document store and the data lake copy is logged. Architecture v5 has no data lake: the lake and Power BI are not connected, INT-19 and INT-20 are removed, and reporting is built from events into rwb-reporting. Version 4 keeps the requirement text word for word, adds the owning service cell for the three surviving reads, and records the contradiction in the section 3.7 note.
evidence: NFR-042 requirement text; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 9 'The data lake and Power BI are not connected (INT-19 and INT-20 removed)' and slide 37; Template and Rules R5.5 DP-17; ADR-018
proposed: At the next NFR baseline, drop 'the data lake copy' from NFR-042 and keep the case store, document store and reporting read model reads; no lake copy is built, so no lake read is logged

title: Concurrency and named-user figures disagree between section 2, NFR-002 and NFR-003 and Architecture v5
source: 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Non Functional Specification v3.docx
description: Three figures stand for the busiest hour. Section 2 gives about 410 users online from 1,234 named users; section 1 and NFR-002 give about 370 staff of 914 named users and NFR-003 about 50 partner users of about 320; Architecture v5 slide 48 gives 414 concurrent staff and 48 concurrent partners (320 total) with about 21 requests a second. The named-user total of 1,234 agrees across the sources; the concurrent split does not. Version 4 keeps every figure as written and records the difference, reading the Architecture v5 figures as the load-test ones.
evidence: NFR section 2 'Online in the busiest hour | About 410'; section 1 'About 370 staff and 50 partner users online in the busiest hour; 1,234 named users'; NFR-002 target 'About 370 staff online in the busiest hour, of 914 named users'; NFR-003 target 'About 50 partner users online in the busiest hour, of about 320 named users'; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 48 '414 concurrent staff at peak', '48 concurrent partner users (320 total)', '~21 req/s'
proposed: Confirm one concurrent-user figure per population for the busiest hour and use it in NFR-002, NFR-003 and the load test; the named-user total of 1,234 stays

title: Owning service not derivable from the Ownership Map for NFR-032
source: 03 Requirements and specifications/Recovery Workbench Non Functional Specification v3.docx
description: NFR-032 is about retired local files and Excel and SharePoint trackers and the read-only archive kept by the Cutover and Go Live Plan. It names no table, endpoint, event, workflow or job, and the Microservice Ownership Map v1 has no cutover object, so no service can be named as its owner without inventing one. Version 4 writes the section R9 placeholder in the owning service cell of that row and names no service.
evidence: NFR-032 requirement and target 'Archive location recorded per file in the Cutover and Go Live Plan'; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Ownership Map v1.xlsx Tables, Endpoints, Events, Workflows and activities and Jobs sheets, with no cutover or archive object; _work/msr/plan/ownership.json
proposed: The Cutover and Go Live Plan names the owner of each archive file, and NFR-032 gets that owner as its owning service cell at the next NFR baseline; no service schema or contract is created for it
